portal-purpose: Jorge built the Audit Portal with ASP.NET Core and Blazor Interactive Server for analytical investigation and operational audit work.
Its permission-controlled workspace combines record search, audit detail, progress views, documents, change history, and workbook exports.
portal-role: Jorge is the sole hands-on developer across the analytical notebooks, data platform, and Audit Portal.
Colleagues contribute practical billing and casework knowledge that informs analytical assumptions and interface design.
portal-ml: The separate machine-learning program investigates predictive scores for human review prioritization.
Portal integration is proposed and requires evaluation, review, and operational approval before use.
data-purpose: Jorge built an extract-based analytical foundation with Python and PySpark preparation, Parquet datasets in Azure Data Lake Storage Gen2, and Synapse serverless SQL access.
It supports SQL investigation, aggregated analysis, and selected downstream application queries.
data-role: Jorge is the sole hands-on developer of the analytical notebooks and data platform, including transformations, prepared datasets, and SQL access structures.
Colleagues contribute billing and casework knowledge to help refine assumptions and requirements.
ml-status: Jorge implemented a supervised-learning program in Python and PySpark for audit prioritization, which remains experimental.
Execution records are needed to substantiate completed evaluations, model selection, and operational readiness.
ml-ranking: Random Forest is configured for continued experimentation, including a fixed fallback path.
The reviewed notebook exports have no execution outputs, so configuration is not a measured model ranking; comparative results remain evaluation requirements.
ml-label: The target predicts whether a review reduction field is populated: zero counts as positive, while null or blank counts as negative.
It reflects a recording convention within reviewed bills, not the amount reduced, fraud, improper billing, or an instruction to initiate a full audit.
ml-framework: The project uses Spark ML with Python and PySpark in Azure Synapse.
Its pipelines combine categorical indexing, encoding, median imputation, and vector assembly, with learned preprocessing fitted within each training fold.
ml-calibration: Jorge implemented Platt calibration using Spark logistic regression, separate calibration and test windows, a delayed-label buffer, and rolling time-based backtests.
Calibration can change probability interpretation without necessarily improving ranking.
background: Jorge's economics and faculty research background led to banking data and business analysis, then analytical infrastructure, experimental models, and applications.
His work connects business questions with data quality, analytical methods, and practical workflows.
research-role: Jorge supported faculty research on profitability forecasting, consumer spending, conjoint analysis, and pricing.
His research assistance is acknowledged in a published 2014 cattle-ranch profitability study.
research-credit: Anand N. Asthana authored the 2014 cattle-ranch profitability study.
Jorge contributed research assistance and is acknowledged as J. Avilés on page 478.
research-methods: The cattle-ranch study uses a vector space model and kernel ridge regression with randomized ten-fold cross-validation.
It investigates the relationship between ranch characteristics and profitability.
